subject: EN

explanation.body: **Signalwörter** verraten die Zeitform: *usually, every day* → Simple Present · *now, at the moment* → Present Progressive · *yesterday, ago, last, in 1997* → Simple Past · *just, already, yet, since, for* → Present Perfect · *while, as* → Past Progressive · *before, by, after* → Past Perfect.

source: Nach Prüfungshefte MSA Englisch Berlin 2026, Training Grammatik (Zeitformen)

from.satz: I usually ___ TV in the evening.
She ___ the piano every day.
Listen! They ___ their grandma right now.
He ___ to work the other day.
I ___ breakfast, then I went to the station.
He ___ with his girlfriend since 2003.
from.grund: *since* = seit einem Zeitpunkt bis heute → **Present Perfect**.

from.satz: I have just ___ at the airport.
I ___ not cleaned my room yet.
She ___ TV all day and she is still watching.
from.grund: *all day* und dauert noch an → **Present Perfect Progressive**.

from.satz: He ___ already finished his homework by 10 pm.
from.grund: *by 10 pm*: fertig vor einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit → **Past Perfect** (had + 3. Form).

from.satz: As she ___ food, her telephone rang.
I was working while John ___ to the park.
I think he ___ at 10 pm.
Who is going to tell her? – I ___.
I ___ marry her. We have already planned the wedding.
If he keeps running like that, he ___ fall over.
We ___ tomorrow at 9 am. The timetable says so.
I ___ to Thailand this week. Everything is booked.
The sun never ___ in the west.
She ___ jogging before she went to bed.
He ___ been waiting for his date for 2 hours.
from.grund: *for 2 hours* bis jetzt → **Present Perfect Progressive** (has been + -ing).

from.satz: I ___ my key! I can't get in.
from.grund: Folge in der Gegenwart (kann nicht rein) → **Present Perfect**.

subject: EN

explanation.body: Simple Present: *usually, always, often, never, every day*. Present Progressive: *now, at the moment, right now, Look!*. Simple Past: *yesterday, ago, last week, in 1997*. Present Perfect: *just, already, yet, ever, since, for, so far*. Past Perfect: *by, before, until that day*.

source: Nach Prüfungshefte MSA Englisch Berlin 2026, Training Grammatik (Signalwörter)

from.bsp: She plays the piano every day.
They are calling grandma at the moment.
I am doing my homework right now.
We moved here two years ago.
I have not cleaned my room yet.
So far we have read three books.
He had finished his homework by 10 pm.
Until that day I had never seen the sea.

subject: EN
prompt: Ergänze die fehlende Form des unregelmäßigen Verbs (Grundform – Simple Past – past participle).

explanation.body: Unregelmäßige Verben musst du **auswendig** lernen. Die 2. Form steht allein (*I went*), die 3. Form immer mit have/has/had (*I have gone*).

source: Nach Prüfungshefte MSA Englisch Berlin 2026, Training Grammatik (Unregelmäßige Verben)

from.voll: wake up – woke up – woken up

subject: EN

explanation.body: **can/could** Fähigkeit, Erlaubnis, Bitte · **may/might** Möglichkeit, höfliche Erlaubnis · **must** Pflicht, starke Empfehlung · **mustn't** Verbot · **needn't** nicht nötig · **should/ought to** Ratschlag, Vermutung · **shall** Angebot · **will/would** Wunsch, Versprechen, Höflichkeit. Ersatzformen: *be able to, be allowed to, have to*.

source: Nach Prüfungshefte MSA Englisch Berlin 2026, Training Grammatik (Modalverben)

from.satz: You ___ smoke here. (Verbot)
from.grund: *must not* drückt ein Verbot aus. Vorsicht: Es ist **nicht** das Gegenteil von must.

from.satz: I ___ swim when I was five. (Fähigkeit in der Vergangenheit)
from.grund: *could* = Vergangenheit von can (Fähigkeit). Ersatzform: *was able to*.

from.satz: ___ I open the window? (höfliche Bitte um Erlaubnis)
from.grund: *May I …?* = höfliche Frage um Erlaubnis (auch *Could I …?*).

from.satz: You ___ call grandma. It's her birthday. (Pflicht)
You ___ call grandma, she is on holiday. (nicht nötig)
from.grund: *need not* = keine Notwendigkeit. Ersatzform: *don't have to*.

from.satz: You ___ speak clearly to her. (Ratschlag)
It ___ be rainy in London. (Möglichkeit, eher unwahrscheinlich)
___ I carry your bags? (Angebot)
He ___ arrive any moment. (Vermutung)
You ___ be angry. (Wahrscheinlichkeit: wahrscheinlich sauer)
from.grund: *must* kann auch Wahrscheinlichkeit ausdrücken: Du bist wahrscheinlich sauer.

from.satz: ___ you please call grandma? (höflicher Wunsch)
from.grund: *Would you please …?* = höfliche Bitte, höflicher als will.

from.satz: I ___ call grandma for you. (höfliches Angebot)
You ___ not call grandma. (Verbot, höflicher als mustn't)
from.grund: *may not* = Verbot, höflicher und weniger energisch als mustn't.

from.satz: Ersatzform für must: You ___ call grandma.
from.grund: *have to* ersetzt must (Pflicht). *be allowed to* = dürfen, *be able to* = können.

subject: EN

explanation.body: **Typ I** (möglich): if + Simple Present, Hauptsatz **will** + Infinitiv. **Typ II** (unwahrscheinlich): if + Simple Past, Hauptsatz **would** + Infinitiv. **Typ III** (unmöglich, Vergangenheit): if + Past Perfect, Hauptsatz **would have** + 3. Form. Komma nur, wenn der if-Satz vorne steht.

source: Nach Prüfungshefte MSA Englisch Berlin 2026, Training Grammatik (If-clauses)

from.satz: I ___ tired tomorrow if I go to bed late today.
from.grund: **Typ I**: if + Simple Present (go), Hauptsatz will-future.

from.satz: If I ___ a superhero, I would save everyone.
from.grund: **Typ II**: if + Simple Past (bei *be* meist *were*), Hauptsatz would + Infinitiv.

from.satz: If I find the time, I ___ you after class.
from.grund: **Typ I**: if + Simple Present, Hauptsatz will + Infinitiv.

from.satz: You ___ the race if you hadn't slowed down.
from.grund: **Typ III**: if + Past Perfect (hadn't slowed), Hauptsatz would have + 3. Form.

from.satz: He would make a lot of money if he ___ his idea.
from.grund: **Typ II**: Hauptsatz would, also if + Simple Past.

from.satz: If it ___ today, I won't go outside.
from.grund: **Typ I**: Im if-Satz steht **nie** will, sondern Simple Present.

from.satz: If I had woken up early, I ___ the train.
from.grund: **Typ III**: Bedauern über die Vergangenheit, would have + 3. Form.

from.satz: If I ___ you, I would wait.
from.grund: **Typ II**, feste Wendung: *If I were you* (Ratschlag).

from.satz: If you break the mirror, you ___ bad luck.
If my grandparents ___, I would not have been born.
If you had a boat, what ___ you name it?
from.grund: **Typ II**: hypothetische Frage, if + Simple Past (had), would.

from.satz: If you don't do your homework, your teacher ___ very angry.

subject: EN
prompt:
Which type of if-clause is this?

„{{s_satz}}“

choices: Typ III: unmöglich, Vergangenheit (Past Perfect + would have)

explanation.body: Schau auf das **Verb im if-Satz**: Simple Present → Typ I, Simple Past → Typ II, Past Perfect (had + 3. Form) → Typ III.

source: Nach Prüfungshefte MSA Englisch Berlin 2026, Training Grammatik (If-clauses)

from.satz: If it rains today, I won't go outside.
from.grund: if + rains (Simple Present), won't go (will-future): vorhersehbare Konsequenz.

from.satz: If I had time, I would come to your party.
from.grund: if + had (Simple Past), would come: Entschuldigung, eher unwahrscheinlich.

from.satz: If you hadn't spent so much time on the PC, your grades might have been better.
from.loesung: Typ III: unmöglich, Vergangenheit (Past Perfect + would have)
from.grund: if + hadn't spent (Past Perfect), might have been: Kritik an der Vergangenheit.

from.satz: If you are nice, I will buy you the toy.
If I were you, I would wait.
from.grund: Ratschlag mit *If I were you*: Simple Past, would.

from.satz: If I had woken up early, I would not have missed the train.
from.loesung: Typ III: unmöglich, Vergangenheit (Past Perfect + would have)
from.grund: Bedauern: had woken (Past Perfect), would not have missed.

from.satz: If you break the mirror, you will have bad luck.
If you had a boat, what would you name it?
If my grandparents had not met, I would not have been born.
from.loesung: Typ III: unmöglich, Vergangenheit (Past Perfect + would have)
from.grund: Hypothese über die Vergangenheit: had not met, would not have been.

subject: EN

explanation.body: Fragen und Verneinungen brauchen **do/does/did** + Grundform (*Does she like …? She doesn't like …*). Ausnahmen: **be** und **Modalverben** (*Is he …? Can you …? He isn't, you can't*) und **have** als Hilfsverb (*Have you ever …?*).

source: Nach Prüfungshefte MSA Englisch Berlin 2026, Training Grammatik

from.grund: Frage im Simple Present: **do** + Subjekt + Grundform.
Verneinung he/she/it: **doesn't** + Grundform (das -s steckt schon in does).

from.a: Did he go to school yesterday?
from.b: Did he went to school yesterday?
from.c: Does he went to school yesterday?
from.grund: Frage im Simple Past: **did** + Grundform (nicht went).
Modalverben brauchen **kein do** und keinen to-Infinitiv.

from.a: Have you ever been to London?
from.b: Did you ever been to London?
from.c: Have you ever went to London?
from.d: Do you ever been to London?
Why did not you call me?

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct form of the adjective.

explanation.body: **Kurze** Adjektive: -er / the -est (*taller, the tallest*; bei -y: *easier*; Konsonant verdoppeln: *bigger, hotter*). **Lange** Adjektive: more / the most (*more interesting*). **Unregelmäßig**: good – better – best, bad – worse – worst, far – farther – farthest. Vergleich mit *than*, Gleichheit mit *as … as*.

source: Rahmenlehrplan Englisch Berlin, Use of English

from.satz: This car is ___ (fast) than mine.
She is the ___ (good) player in the team.
This film is ___ (interesting) than the book.
Tom is ___ (tall) than his brother.
It's the ___ (bad) day of my life.
My bag is ___ (heavy) than yours.
This is the ___ (expensive) phone in the shop.
Berlin is ___ (big) than Hamburg.
He is as ___ (old) as me.
This test was ___ (easy) than the last one.
She runs ___ (far) than I do.
It's ___ (hot) today than yesterday.
